label: Executive Order 12850 of May 28, 1993 (National Archives)
Executive Order 12850 (Clinton White House archive)
notes: The order requires the Secretary of State to recommend against extending Most-Favored-Nation status for China after July 3, 1994 unless China is complying with the freedom of emigration objectives and the 1992 prison-labor agreement, and then makes progress 'overall, significant progress' on further listed human-rights areas.

label: Human Rights Watch/Asia: China, no progress on human rights (May 4, 1994)
Amnesty International: Wei Jingsheng held in secret for 16 months (August 4, 1995)
notes: NGO reports: HRW names Wei Jingsheng among those 'silenced' and mentions Shattuck; Amnesty says Wei Jingsheng was held in secret for 16 months as of August 1995, which counts back to spring 1994. The exact arrest date, April 1, 1994, and the link to the Shattuck meeting are not in the snippets.

label: The President's News Conference, May 26, 1994 (Clinton White House archive)
Public Papers of the Presidents, 1994, Book I, p. 991 (govinfo)
notes: Clinton's remarks: Secretary Christopher reported on the conditions in last year's executive order; 'there was progress made in important areas, including the resolution of all emigration cases, the establishment of a memorandum' on prison labor, though China did not make overall significant progress in all the areas; Clinton decided to renew MFN anyway.

label: S. Res. 148, 104th Congress: sense of the Senate on the arrest of Harry Wu (govinfo)
notes: Senate resolution recitals: Peter H. Wu, known as Harry Wu, spent 19 years in Chinese labor camps and was arrested in 1995 on entering China. His departure for the United States in 1985 was not in the snippet; Britannica returned HTTP 403.
Only Britannica was offered and it returned HTTP 403. Wu's covert filming and the 1991 60 Minutes broadcast are unchecked.

label: Statement by the White House Press Secretary on the expulsion of Harry Wu, August 24, 1995 (Clinton White House archive)
Amnesty International: Ding Zilin arrested, Harry Wu sentenced
notes: White House statement: the PRC 'has expelled Harry Wu from the country'; 'Wu was convicted on Aug. 24 and sentenced to 15 years imprisonment.' Amnesty's bulletin on the sentence is dated 23 August 1995, so a one-day discrepancy exists between sources about the conviction date; 'espionage' as the charge is not in the snippets.

label: Federal Register, January 24, 2002: notices of Trade Adjustment Assistance petitions (Magnequench, Anderson, Indiana)
USCC statement of Commissioner Carolyn Bartholomew (Magnequench and rare-earth magnets)
notes: A Labor Department notice lists a worker-adjustment petition by Magnequench workers in Indiana (petition dates in November 2001); the Commission statement discusses China's acquisition of the bonded-magnet maker. notes: US congressional commission analysis: the Chinese government dismissed as 'illegal and invalid' the Dalai Lama's May 1995 recognition of Gedun Choekyi Nyima and installed Gyaltsen Norbu in December 1995. The golden-urn lottery in November is not in the text read.
